subject: design
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Concept of the skill, Coverage, Philosophy, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and canonical journey-mapping practice (customer journey map, emotional curve / moments of truth, service blueprint with line of visibility and back-stage, current vs future state, research grounding).

cases.scenario: A team kicks off a 'checkout journey map' by listing the five checkout screens in order and labeling each with the UI action that happens on it.
cases.context: They believe the ordered screen list is the journey map and are ready to start redesigning screens.
cases.question: How should the agent respond?
expected_flags: Flags the screen list as a task flow, not a journey map
Notes the missing emotional curve, cross-channel/time span, and back-stage layer
Adds user-perspective stages and lanes for actions, thoughts, and feelings
Insists on grounding pain points in research and naming opportunity areas at specific stages
expected_fix_hints: Reframe stages from the user's perspective and add an emotional curve
Identify moments of truth and back-stage dependencies before redesigning screens
absent_signals: Do not accept the bare screen list as a journey map
Do not jump to per-screen redesign without the experience arc

cases.scenario: A SaaS product loses many customers during a multi-day onboarding that spans automated email, the web app, and a human customer-success call. Leadership wants to know where to invest.
cases.context: Churn is concentrated but the team cannot agree on which step causes it.
cases.question: How should the agent map this to locate the moment of truth?
expected_flags: Lays onboarding out as stages over multiple days and across the three channels
Plots an emotional curve to locate the trough where churn is decided
Adds a service-blueprint back-stage layer (CS rep, systems, support processes) below the line of visibility
Grounds the trough in evidence (support logs, interviews) and names opportunity areas there
expected_fix_hints: Build a cross-channel timeline with actions/thoughts/feelings lanes
Add the back-stage layer for the moments that depend on hidden handoffs
absent_signals: Do not optimize a single screen in isolation
Do not assert the cause without research grounding

cases.scenario: A stakeholder shares a future-state journey map where every stage has a positive verb ('delighted', 'empowered') and the emotional curve is a smooth upward wave with no dips.
cases.context: No research was cited; the map was drafted in a single workshop from intuition.
cases.question: How should the agent critique and improve the map?
expected_flags: Identifies the anodyne happy-path failure mode — it describes hopes, not research
Requires real lows in the emotional curve; a curve with no dips omits the hard parts
Demands each pain point/trough cite a research source
Names specific opportunity areas at the troughs rather than generic praise
expected_fix_hints: Ground the map in synthesis output before treating it as decision-ready
Re-plot the curve from evidence, exposing the troughs
absent_signals: Do not accept an all-positive curve as credible
Do not treat an unresearched map as a redesign brief

cases.scenario: A retail experience lets a customer return an online order to a physical store. Returns frequently fail at the counter even though every screen and email looks fine in isolation.
cases.context: The failure seems to live in handoffs between the web system, the warehouse, and the in-store POS that the customer never sees.
cases.question: What kind of map should the agent build and why?
expected_flags: Chooses a service blueprint because the failure lives in back-stage handoffs
Draws the line of visibility explicitly, separating front-stage from back-stage
Includes both human and system actors in the back-stage steps (web system, warehouse, POS)
Maps the cross-channel experience over time (online → physical store)
expected_fix_hints: Extend the journey map downward into back-stage and support processes
Locate the handoff that breaks and name it as an opportunity area
absent_signals: Do not stop at the front-stage screens and emails
Do not draw a system architecture diagram in place of the experience map

cases.scenario: An exec asks for 'one journey map of the whole product' to align the leadership team, while a designer wants a detailed map to drive a specific onboarding redesign.
cases.context: The team has time and budget for one mapping effort, not two.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the map(s)?
expected_flags: Matches granularity to the decision the map will inform
A board-level alignment map is intentionally coarser than a redesign brief
Recommends distinct artifacts/zoom levels for distinct decisions rather than one map serving both
Distinguishes current-state (document reality, surface pain) from future-state (propose redesign, align stakeholders)
expected_fix_hints: Produce a coarse lifecycle map for alignment and a zoomed-in moment-of-truth map for the redesign
Pick scope (single transaction vs lifecycle vs one moment) per decision
absent_signals: Do not force one granularity to serve two different decisions
Do not default to maximum detail regardless of the decision

cases.scenario: A PM asks the journey-mapping owner to (a) decompose the steps inside the file-upload modal, (b) draw the microservice call graph for the checkout API, and (c) define the site's top-level navigation structure.
cases.context: The team treats 'journey mapping' as the home for all flow, system, and structure diagrams.
cases.question: How should the agent scope these requests?
expected_flags: Single-modal step decomposition is out of scope — that is task-analysis
A microservice call graph is system topology, not human experience — an engineering artifact, not a journey map
Top-level navigation structure is out of scope — that is information-architecture
Offers the in-scope part: the cross-channel experience arc, emotional curve, and back-stage where relevant
expected_fix_hints: Redirect modal steps to task-analysis, the call graph to engineering/architecture, and nav structure to information-architecture
Deliver the experience-over-time map for the parts that are genuinely journeys
absent_signals: Do not decompose the upload modal here
Do not draw the microservice topology or the navigation tree as a journey map

cases.scenario: A team wants to build a journey map for a new audience segment they have never interviewed, planning to fill the actions/thoughts/feelings lanes from team assumptions.
cases.context: No qualitative research exists yet for this segment, but the deadline is tight.
cases.question: How should the agent proceed?
expected_flags: States that an unresearched journey map is fiction
Recommends running user-research and research-synthesis first
Refuses to present an assumption-filled map as decision-ready
Notes that map credibility comes from grounding in synthesis output
expected_fix_hints: Sequence research → synthesis → map rather than assumption → map
If a draft is needed, mark every assumed element as unvalidated pending research
absent_signals: Do not fill the lanes from team intuition and call it grounded
Do not treat the assumption-based map as a redesign brief
